Polity Engine Atlas

How the simulation runs, mechanic by mechanic: the modules a run goes through, the fixed order of one tick, what each mechanic reads and decides, and a recorded run replayed tick by tick. Every reference opens the exact line on GitHub.

How a run works

A run is a pure sequence: build the world once, then repeat the same 14 phases every tick, then summarise. One tick is a quarter of a year; the defaults run 30 years (121 ticks, 0 to 120 inclusive) with 100 citizens.

    2 · Every tick ticks 0 … total

      The phase order is load-bearing (docstring at ): each phase reads what the earlier ones wrote this tick, and opinion dynamics run last so the next tick reads the moved views.

      3 · After the run

        Which engine you get depends on the config. llm.enabled ships false, and with no LLM client every decision falls back to the deterministic rules in simple_rules.py; most mechanics also ship switched off. The runner's flagship profile turns the institutions on; exploration adds the agents (president, nominees, forum, coalition leaders, amendments). The replay on the third tab is an exploration run on the LLM engine.

        The modules

        Every module under api/domain/polity/ that a run touches, grouped by role. Pick one to see what it does and what it calls.

        The calendar

        Elections and rotations are pure arithmetic on the tick (). Two presidential terms at the defaults: president every 16 ticks, legislature offset by 8, the sortition chamber reseated every 4, a snapshot of every citizen once a year.

        Inside one tick

        The 14 phases of TICK_PHASES, in the order they run. Chips open the mechanic.

        The accountability loop

        The circuit most mechanics belong to: an election seats a president, their drift opens a gap with each citizen, the gap (with emotions, events and neighbours) decides who is consulted, the consulted put pressure on, pressure erodes legitimacy, and a lost confidence vote recalls them and reopens the vote. Click a station.
